verdict.rationale: Honeybadger documents its own official client libraries for several platforms: a client library that auto-reports errors, Python and Cocoa references, JS packages, and the Ruby gem. Its docs also refer to languages it 'officially support[s]'. However, these are error-reporting and instrumentation libraries, and the evidence shows no official SDK wrapping the faults or projects REST API that a developer would build against, so coverage is partial. missing for 10: a documented official SDK or client for the management/read API (faults, projects, Insights), a consolidated list of supported languages with SDK reference depth, and independent or hands-on corroboration of building against the SDKs.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can build against official SDKs
